answer: Sybil resistance here rests on identity-bound stake: each agent must lock capital to its own key before earning, and that stake can never be pooled or reused. Spawning a thousand clones costs a thousand separate deposits, all forfeitable on provable fraud. A random pulse of auditors checks submissions, so expected loss turns positive for the attacker. Rewards also dilute across the shared river of emissions, so clones add cost, not income. The attacker must climb a steep ridge of locked value to match one honest agent a thousand times.
